publication: Daily Record (Morristown, NJ) - USA Today Network New Jersey, 'Matters of Fact' column by Jim Beckerman
summary: Feature 'Reporter had to fight his own war' profiles Ollie Stewart, the first Black war correspondent accredited in WWII, who reported for the New Jersey Afro-American (Newark); includes history of the paper as a Black-owned chain founded 1892 and based in Baltimore, and promotes a May 23, 2023 program on Stewart at Newark Public Library.

people.name: Ollie Stewart
people.role: AFRO/New Jersey Afro-American war correspondent, first accredited Black WWII correspondent; from Louisiana, partly schooled in East Orange, NJ; wrote for the paper until his death in 1977 in Paris

people.name: Benjamin O. Davis Jr.
people.role: US Air Force general, commander of the WWII Tuskegee Airmen, first African American brigadier general in the Air Force (pictured with Stewart)

people.name: Larry Greene
people.role: professor of history at Seton Hall University, hosting program 'Fighting on Two Fronts: Black GIs in World War II and Ollie Stewart's Reporting in the NJ Afro-American'

people.name: Savannah Wood
people.role: great-great-granddaughter of the New Jersey Afro-American's founder, manager of the archives

people.name: Jimmy Richardson
people.role: Paterson historian who has written about the New Jersey Afro-American and other Black papers

people.name: Marc Lancaster
people.role: wrote about Stewart on the website 'World War II on Deadline'

people.name: Mrs. Carter
people.role: Newark resident (27 N. Peach Street) whose son Sgt. James H. Carter was reported seen by Stewart in Africa

people.name: Isaac Woodard
people.role: Black veteran featured on the cover of the New Jersey Afro-American's 1946 'Year of Great Negro Resistance to Hate Groups' issue

people.name: Jim Beckerman
people.role: Daily Record/NorthJersey.com columnist, author of this article

incidents.what: New Jersey Afro-American publishes 'Year of Great Negro Resistance to Hate Groups' issue featuring Isaac Woodard
Program 'Fighting on Two Fronts: Black GIs in World War II and Ollie Stewart's Reporting in the NJ Afro-American' at Newark Public Library, co-sponsored by NJPAC and the Newark History Society
Ollie Stewart dies in Paris; continued writing for the Afro-American until his death

connections: New Jersey Afro-American (Newark) - Black-owned weekly, founded 1892, part of the Baltimore-based AFRO chain, ceased NJ edition; celebrated 130 years of continuous operation
Chicago Defender and Pittsburgh Courier named as peer Black-owned papers
